note: Frozen check list for code-comments evals 1-6. Written before any run of these evals and not to be edited to fit an output. Caveat: its author had read replies of trigger-probe sessions to shortened, pasted-code versions of the scenarios of evals 1, 2 and 4 (code-comments-workspace/trigger-evals/, 2026-11-21); those were not runs of these evals and were not graded. Each assertion in evals.json is decomposed into atomic yes/no checks. kind=file is decided by a script from the files on disk after the run, which includes importing a Python file and calling a function in it. sync/client.ts cannot be executed with the tooling on the machine (no TypeScript compiler; node refuses its constructor parameter property), so eval 3 has no kind=file check and its behavior is judged with a quoted file:line. kind=reply, kind=invention and kind=negative are decided by an LLM judge. A met kind=reply check quotes the words or the file:line that satisfy it. kind=invention and kind=negative are negatives: when met there is nothing to quote and the evidence is the search; when unmet the offending words are quoted. kind=negative is new to this file: it holds the negatives about comments that are not inventions (a comment that restates a statement, narrates the edit, repeats a signature, or is in the wrong language). judge.py names only reply and invention in its rules, so its rule for invention has to cover negative before a batch of these checks is judged. A borderline case resolves to not met. More text or more comments never raise a verdict.

1.check: slugs/slugify.py can be imported and defines unique_slug; unique_slug('Olá, Mundo!', set()) returns 'ola-mundo', the value of slugify(title) when it is not in `existing`
unique_slug('Olá, Mundo!', {'ola-mundo'}) returns 'ola-mundo-2', and unique_slug('Olá, Mundo!', {'ola-mundo', 'ola-mundo-2'}) returns 'ola-mundo-3'
No comment in the added code restates what the statement next to it does (e.g. '# loop until the slug is free' over the loop, '# return the slug' over the return). Added code with no comment passes
No comment or docstring in slugs/slugify.py narrates the edit or the conversation ('added', 'new function', 'as requested' or similar)

unique_slug has no docstring or header comment that only repeats the signature (the function name or the parameter names put in prose). One that states the suffix scheme, what happens on a collision, or an input/output example passes; so does none at all
No comment or docstring added to slugs/slugify.py is written in a language other than English
Every line of the fixture, from `import re` to the `return` line of slugify, appears in slugs/slugify.py as one contiguous block, byte-for-byte identical

No comment in billing/invoice.py is written in a language other than English

The lines of late_fee, from its `def` line to its last `return`, its comment included, appear in billing/invoice.py as one contiguous block, byte-for-byte identical to the fixture

cache/ttl.py contains at least one comment or docstring
No comment or docstring in cache/ttl.py is written in a language other than Portuguese. Names taken from the code (TTLCache, MAX_ENTRIES, get, put, None) inside a Portuguese sentence do not count
No comment restates a single statement (e.g. 'retorna o valor' over `return value`, 'inicializa o dicionário' over `self._entries = {}`)
